chapterTitle: FBISE Model Paper 1 (Section A Simulator - Units 1-5)
subject: physics-9

questions.question: The word science is derived from _______word scientia.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Latin. The word “science” comes from the Latin word scientia. It means knowledge or understanding.

questions.question: _________ is the study of matter, energy and their interaction.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): physics. Physics studies matter, energy and how they interact.It explains natural physical phenomenon.

questions.question: Least count of vernier caliper is _________.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 0.01 cm. Least count is the smallest value a vernier caliper can measure. For a standard vernier caliper, it is 0.01 cm.

questions.question: One tera is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 1012. The prefix tera (T) represents 10¹² (one trillion), while 10⁻¹² is pico (p).

questions.question: ________telescope orbits around the earth and provide information about stars.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Hubble Space. The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth. It provides detailed Information about stars and galaxies.

questions.question: If zero line of Vernier scale is on the left side of the zero of the main scale then zero error is __________.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): negative. If the zero line of the Vernier scale lies to the left of the main scale zero mark, the zero error is negative.

questions.question: If zero of circular scale has crossed the index line, then zero error will be ___.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): negative. When the circular scale zero mark crosses the index line, the zero error of a screw gauge is negative.

questions.question: 0.00078 has ____significant figures.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 2. Leading zeros are not significant; only digits 7 and 8 are significant (2 significant figures).

questions.question: Which of the following is a base quantity?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Length'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 1 (Physical Quantities & Measurement), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If you're calculating the speed of a runner, which base quantity are you utilizing?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 'Time'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 1 (Physical Quantities & Measurement), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: When determining the pressure inside a balloon, which base quantity are you considering?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Force'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 1 (Physical Quantities & Measurement), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which of the following is a derived quantity in mechanics?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Energy'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 1 (Physical Quantities & Measurement), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.
